tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on Harborview demo: PDFTron outlines ALL text, zero room labels found. v2 = (a) productize M3 tiles lane as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action; (b) callout-vs-room filtering.

prep.what: Productize the M3 vision tile-based label reader as an opt-in action, and add callout-vs-room noise filtering.
prep.understand: The free live-text lane works for firms like Holabird (92/109 rooms named) but fails for PDF-outlined-text firms like Harborview. The M3 tiles lane solves this via vision OCR over image tiles (~4.3 min/sheet, costs money via metered credits). The second half is filtering: Holabird shows false matches — UP arrows, FEC callouts, paragraph notes — that match as room names.
approach: Locate the M3 tiles lane spike (docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py) and understand the tile-generation + MiniMax vision call structure
Wire the lane into the service as an opt-in action gated behind the §7a metered-credits event; add a 'read labels (AI)' endpoint or flag
Add MINIMAX_AI key to VPS .env (the secrets decision: key must reach aztakeoff.azteamai.com to work in prod)
Build callout-vs-room filtering rules in the label post-processor: reject all-caps short strings (e.g. 'FEC', 'UP'), long paragraph-like text, and directional words documented in R13

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite already scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py. Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build the full assembly system: map room classification → a set of quantities (flooring SF, wall paint SF, baseboard LF, etc.) using room geometry + wall height, and emit them into the Excel export.
prep.understand: engine/assemblies.py has a scaffold. Each classification maps to a set of assembly lines — one classification can produce 8+ quantities. Wall heights aren't in the 2D plan geometry; they need a default-ft value (likely a config param) with optional per-room override. Quantity formulas: floor_sf = room area, wall_sf = perimeter × height, baseboard = perimeter, ceiling = floor_sf. CSI MasterFormat is the reference for category naming.
approach: Open engine/assemblies.py and understand the current scaffold shape (what's stubbed, what's wired)
Build the classification → assemblies lookup (a dict or YAML config): map 'bedroom', 'bathroom', 'hallway', etc. to their assembly lines with quantity formulas
Add wall_height support: read a project-level default (from the service config/sheet params), apply per-room override if present, compute wall_sf = perimeter × wall_height
Wire the output into engine/excel.py — add assembly columns to the existing 5-tab workbook, keeping the gauntlet green (run pytest + gauntlet after each slice)
resources: engine/assemblies.py — the existing scaffold to extend
engine/excel.py — the 5-tab workbook builder to wire quantities into
CSI MasterFormat Divisions 03-09 — reference for assembly category naming
docs/spike/ — geometry and measurement reference patterns
service pytest suite + gauntlet — run after each slice to stay green

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Must land before t48 (trade pricing) can price trim/LF measurements from the takeoff.

prep.what: Add a `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` entry to the RateType enum and wire it through the factory and seeder so trim can be priced per linear foot.
prep.understand: RateType drives how LineItemFactory assigns a unit to a seeded estimate line. Right now only sqft and per-unit are supported. Trim and baseboard measurements come in as linear feet (LF) — without this enum case, the factory can't assign the right unit and the seeder falls back to a generic custom line.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to app/Enums/RateType.php with a human label 'Per Linear Foot'
Add `'per_linear_ft' => 'lf'` mapping to LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()
Add a painting/trim LaborRate seed row in LaborRateSeeder (per_linear_ft, for trim/baseboard)
Run `php artisan db:seed --class=LaborRateSeeder` locally and verify the row appears correctly
resources: app/Enums/RateType.php — add the new case here
app/Services/LineItemFactory.php — unitFromRateType() method
database/seeders/LaborRateSeeder.php — add the trim labor row

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add wall height input + compute perimeter × height per room. The seeder currently DROPS geometry — preserve it.

prep.what: Add a project-level wall height field and compute wall paint SF per room (perimeter × wall_height) in the TakeoffEstimateSeeder, producing a 'Wall paint area' line for each room.
prep.understand: The geometry/perimeter data IS returned by the takeoff engine per room, but TakeoffEstimateSeeder currently drops it. Wall height is not in the 2D plan — it must be a user-provided project default (e.g., 9ft) with optional per-room override. Wall paint SF = meta.perimeter × wall_height_ft. The derived wall area becomes the painting labor/material basis (t46 routes it to the painting trade).
approach: Add wall_height (nullable float, project-level default) to the estimates table via migration; add the column to Estimate model fillable and the TakeoffController data flow
Fix TakeoffEstimateSeeder to preserve geometry (meta.perimeter / geometry.rings) for each room instead of dropping it
In the seeder loop, compute wall_sf = meta.perimeter × (room.wall_height ?? estimate.wall_height ?? 9.0) for each room
Emit a 'Wall paint area' line per room (kind=derived_wall, unit=sqft) — this feeds t46's trade routing
Add the wall_height field to the Vue Review widget so the user can set it before seeding
resources: TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php — the seeder to fix and extend
app/Models/Estimate.php — add wall_height column and fillable
resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue (or TakeoffReview component) — add the wall height input
Takeoff engine geometry docs or service/routes.py — understand meta.perimeter field shape
Holabird takeoff project in prod for testing the actual output

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement currently collapses to one anonymous kind=custom $0 line, dropping kind + geometry. Switch on kind: area→flooring, derived wall SF→painting, line(LF)→trim, count(EA)→doors.

prep.what: In TakeoffEstimateSeeder, replace the single-line collapse with a switch on measurement kind, routing each measurement type to the correct trade and calling the right LineItemFactory method.
prep.understand: Right now all takeoff data becomes one $0 custom line — the trade routing seam is completely unimplemented. The core-vs-subbed helper (ProjectType::isCoreTrade()) tells us painting and flooring are own-team, while trim/tile/doors are subcontracted (Rafa's rule). Each kind maps to: 'area'→flooring (sqft, own-team), derived wall SF→painting (sqft, own-team), 'line'→trim/baseboard (lf, subbed), 'count'→door/window counts (ea, subbed).
approach: Understand the measurement JSON shape from the engine (the `kind` field values: 'area', 'line', 'count') by checking service/routes.py or existing seeder code

Add a switch/match in TakeoffEstimateSeeder on measurement.kind, routing to: flooring LineItemFactory call (area), painting LineItemFactory call (derived_wall), fromSubcontract call (line/count trades)
Use ProjectType::isCoreTrade() to set is_subcontracted correctly on each routed line
Test by seeding a real takeoff project (Holabird is good) and verifying the estimate lines have the right kinds and trades
resources: TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php — the main file to rework
app/Services/LineItemFactory.php — fromMaterial(), fromLaborRate(), fromSubcontract() methods
app/Enums/ProjectType.php — isCoreTrade() / group() helper
Takeoff engine measurement kinds — check service/routes.py or the Vue review widget for what 'kind' values come through
Holabird takeoff in prod (ct-pros instance) for live test
